Here’s a quick rundown of the long‑weekend holidays in Canada for 2023 (dates that fall on a weekday will create a three‑day weekend; if they fall on a weekend, the holiday is typically observed on the nearest weekday):

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend? |
|---------|-------------|-------------|---------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 | Sun | Observed Mon 2 |
| Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario) | Feb 20 | Mon | Yes |
| Louis Riel Day (Manitoba) | Feb 20 | Mon | Yes |
| Heritage Day (New Brunswick) | Feb 20 | Mon | Yes |
| St. Patrick’s Day (Ontario) | Mar 17 | Wed | Yes |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 | Fri | Yes |
| Easter Monday (Quebec, Ontario) | Apr 10 | Mon | Yes |
| Victoria Day | May 22 | Mon | Yes |
| National Indigenous Peoples Day (Northwest Territories, Nunavut) | Jun 21 | Mon | Yes |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 | Tue | Yes |
| Civic Holiday (Ontario, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island) | Aug 7 | Mon | Yes |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 | Mon | Yes |
| Thanksgiving (Canada) | Oct 9 | Mon | Yes |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 | Mon | Yes |
| Christmas Day | Dec 25 | Mon | Yes |
| Boxing Day | Dec 26 | Tue | Yes |

**Key points for your app:**

- **Observance rules:** If a holiday falls on a weekend, most provinces observe it on the following Monday (or preceding Friday for Good Friday).  
- **Province‑specific holidays:** Some holidays (e.g., Family Day, Louis Riel Day, Heritage Day, St. Patrick’s Day, Civic Holiday) vary by province.  
- **Long‑weekends:** A “long weekend” is typically defined as a holiday that creates a three‑day weekend (holiday + weekend). For holidays that fall on a weekday, the holiday itself plus the adjacent weekend days form the long weekend.  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the same information broken down by province or if you need additional details such as public holiday observances for 2024!
